sources.title: Higher-Form Symmetries in 5d

evidence.text: Screen noncompact M2-brane line operators by compact M2-brane particles. Use the long exact sequence of the manifold-boundary pair and Poincaré–Lefschetz duality to express the resulting quotient through relative homology or cohomology.

sources.title: Generalized Symmetries in F-theory and the Topology of Elliptic Fibrations

evidence.text: Use the long exact sequence of (X,∂X), Mayer-Vietoris sequences and elliptic monodromy to compute boundary torsion. For elliptic K3s over C with multiple discriminant points, the stated formula is h^(2) ≅ Tor coker(T−1), with T the ordered total monodromy.

sources.title: Higher-Form Symmetries in 5d

evidence.text: An alternative argument uses asymptotic C-field fluxes and boundary torsion linking pairings. Choosing which torsion fluxes to specify implements choices of gauging; wrapped charge operators reproduce the expected linking phases with probe lines.

sources.title: Higher-Form Symmetries in 5d

evidence.text: Represent compact divisor–curve intersections by integer matrices and compute Smith normal forms. For glued blown-up Hirzebruch surfaces, construct the complex Z^Nd → Z^Nc → Z^Ng from intersections and gluing relations; its middle homology gives Γ ⊕ Z^f.

sources.title: Generalized Symmetries in F-theory and the Topology of Elliptic Fibrations

evidence.text: Construct Lefschetz thimbles and compact rational representatives using intersection pairings and Smith normal forms of negative Cartan matrices. Coefficients descend to Q/Z; replacing fibral curves by their ruled Cartan divisors constructs Pontryagin-dual divisors.

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Integrate the proposed trajectory, restrict its parameters, differentiate to reconstruct η and ξ, and evaluate the spectral formulas. Keep the trajectory family, endpoint prescription and slow-roll truncation explicit when comparing resulting bounds.

sources.title: Eternal Chaotic Inflation is Prohibited by Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Compare the eternal threshold separately with each independent ceiling, then impose both parameter conditions together. The abstraction preserves which quantities are fixed during the field scan and which vary when observational normalization is subsequently imposed.

sources.title: Eternal Chaotic Inflation is Prohibited by Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Compare changes of the physically relevant observable rather than comparing a single component's kick with its drift. In this paper the observable is total potential energy, whose fluctuation scales as √n and whose classical change scales as n.

sources.title: Eternal Chaotic Inflation is Prohibited by Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Starting with identical-field FRW evolution, discard kinetic and acceleration terms under the two slow-roll conditions. Differentiate the resulting Hubble relation and use the quoted density-perturbation formula to connect background drift, fluctuations, and the eternal-inflation criterion.

sources.title: Eternal Chaotic Inflation is Prohibited by Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Estimate fluctuation gradients at the horizon scale, sum their energies, and compare the result with the homogeneous potential energy. Substituting the relevant monomial potential turns this comparison into an upper bound on the common field amplitude.

sources.title: The Swampland Spectrum Conjecture in Inflation

evidence.text: How are multifield inflationary paths and their ordinary field excursions defined? Homogeneous fields evolve under a potential with Hubble friction on a curved, positive-definite target space.

sources.title: The Swampland Spectrum Conjecture in Inflation

evidence.text: Modular j-inflation supplies a curved two-field example for comparing a path in the upper half-plane with its lift to a potential surface. Its potential is modular invariant and its kinetic geometry is hyperbolic.

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: Can a nonsymmetric model enter hyperinflation after an initially stable slow-roll phase? Here negative curvature destabilises the transverse direction as the quadratic potential becomes relatively steeper during descent.

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: Does a three-field evolution reproduce the analytic dependence on transverse speed? The reported numerical example follows the sum π_w1²+π_w2² rather than identifying either component with the two-field transverse velocity.

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Does a common attractor describe sustained two-field inflation with strongly nongeodesic motion across different field-space geometries and potentials? The paper seeks a background construction and a conditional linear stability criterion.

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Can rapid turning occur without negative field-space curvature? The imported flat model combines radial stabilization with an angular slope and supplies such an example.

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: How can a heavy transverse field participate in inflation? Negative field-space curvature can destabilize ordinary slow roll and support a displaced turning trajectory in the imported minimal-geometry model.

sources.title: Attractors, Bifurcations and Curvature in Multi-field Inflation

evidence.text: Can late-time nongeodesic inflationary attractors be described by one effective-potential framework, including their stability and bifurcations, and can stable turning solutions exist without an isometry along the inflationary direction?

sources.title: Scaling attractors in multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Which background trajectories can attract two-field inflation when field-space geometry competes with the potential gradient? The paper organizes constant-epsilon trajectories as critical points, including gradient flow and motion with a stationary transverse coordinate.

evidence.text: Which curved two-field scalar theories admit attracting inflationary trajectories outside slow-roll slow-turn motion, and how are transitions between geodesic and turning motion organized?

evidence.text: Given a scalar potential and field-space metric, which regions admit sustained slow-roll, rapid-turn inflation with arbitrarily many fields, and can those regions be identified without evolving every candidate trajectory?

sources.title: The Swampland Spectrum Conjecture in Inflation

evidence.text: Differentiate the embedding, compute ambient tangent-vector inner products, and integrate the resulting curve speed. The paper uses this standard operation with a potential graph; the operation does not independently justify the graph's physical significance.

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: Construct and evolve the complete quadratic fluctuation operator. A negative mass contribution diagnoses a possible instability; in rotating frames the connection-induced derivative and mass terms must also be retained.

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: The author integrates an approximate growing eigenvalue of rescaled modes v^I = a delta phi^I. The detailed integration is attributed to a forthcoming reference and is not reproduced here.

sources.title: Attractors, Bifurcations and Curvature in Multi-field Inflation

evidence.text: An advection equation for the coordinate transformation, solvable by characteristics once attractor velocities are functions of fields, constructs stationary transverse coordinates. This is distinct from merely choosing an adiabatic/entropic basis.

sources.title: Scaling attractors in multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Project normalized coordinate velocities along and perpendicular to the metric isometry, then search for zeros of the two component-flow equations.

sources.title: Two-field constant roll inflation

evidence.text: The reconstruction strategy first integrates a constant-roll equation for H, obtaining the background geometry independently of the matter split. Einstein equations then determine V(t)=3H²+Ḣ and total kinetic quantity X=−2Ḣ.

sources.title: A geometrical instability for ultra-light fields during inflation?

evidence.text: When does negative field-space curvature produce a physical instability of inflationary isocurvature modes, rather than identify a repulsive background trajectory, and how does the answer differ for heavy and ultra-light spectator fields?

sources.title: Inflation with strongly non-geodesic motion: theoretical motivations and observational imprints

evidence.text: How does strongly non-geodesic inflation arise in negatively curved field space, how does it permit inflation on Planck-steep potentials, and what naturalness limitations and primordial observational signatures accompany it?

sources.title: Hyper-Non-Gaussianities in Inflation with Strongly Nongeodesic Motion

evidence.text: How does strongly nongeodesic inflation in negatively curved field space affect nonlinear curvature perturbations, and can their non-Gaussianities constrain proposed inflationary attractors?

sources.title: Anisotropic hyperbolic inflation

evidence.text: How does a gauge field alter hyperbolic inflation's attractors and slow-roll destabilization, and how can trajectories transition between anisotropic slow-roll and anisotropic hyperbolic regimes?

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: How does field-space geometry change inflationary motion and fluctuation masses? A small curvature radius L permits rapid trajectory turning and can induce instabilities transverse to otherwise slow-roll motion.

evidence.text: Can turning multifield trajectories satisfy proposed quantum-gravity restrictions that are difficult for canonical single-field slow roll?

evidence.text: Does the tachyonic orthogonal entropy mode in Fibre Inflation signal a physical instability, despite a stable single-field background, or does its growth arise from an unsuitable entropy variable?

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by several scalar coordinates whose kinetic terms define a curved field space. Background trajectories and distances depend on this metric, while perturbations probe both its curvature and the potential.
